newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures ease in tandem with dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures ease in tandem with dollar.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures ended lower across the board in thin trade on Friday, with the dollar's tumble more than offsetting an advance in London overnight, traders said.
"Market players might turn into buyers when prices fall below 205 yen," said a trader at a major trading house.
"Trading houses were sellers from the opening. Later we also saw stop-loss selling by individual investors due to the dollar's decline," the trader said.
TOCOM yen-based aluminium futures ranged from 1.4 yen to 2.4 yen per kg lower.
Benchmark October 1998 showed the largest loss of 2.4 yen, closing at 205.8 yen. Trade volume remained thin at 2,974 lots, up slightly from 2,331 lots on Thursday.

Traders said weakness in the dollar, which slipped to below 123 yen for the first time since April 4, weighed on the market, even though dollar-based aluminium prices advanced to trade at $1,670 overnight in London.
Traders they were bracing for further rises towards $1,700 after the metal cleared resistance at $1,650 earlier this week.
Though the metal has reached levels which could trigger sales by producers, such selling is expected to be overwhelmed by fund buying against a backdrop of declining stocks, they said.
